correctness.rationale: The centered disphenoid vertices have pairwise angles with cosine 2p_i-1, each twice. Haar central-plane crossings yield E N=2/pi sum_i arccos(2p_i-1), where N in {3,4}; hence P(triangle)=4/pi sum_i asin(sqrt(p_i))-2. For x>y with third simplex coordinate z>0, x(1-x)-y(1-y)=(x-y)z>0 implies f′(x)<f′(y) for f(t)=asin sqrt(t), establishing strict pairwise-balancing Schur concavity even for x>1/2. Taylor f″(1/3)=-9sqrt(2)/16 gives quadratic gap 9sqrt(2)/(8pi)*sum eps_i², and f(eps)~sqrt(eps) gives uniform nonvertex cusp 4sqrt(eps)/pi. Normal sign decomposition matches independent half-normal triangle inequalities. Independent angular and perturbative checks corroborate but are not used as general proof.
residual_risks: Only nondegenerate equifacial tetrahedra with centroid-zero Haar planes, not arbitrary affine planes or orthogonal shadows.
